data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["The panel's 'commission' errors may be more frequent than the expert's 'omission' errors in highly atypical cases."],"overturn_conditions":["Evidence that commission errors are more catastrophic than omission errors in the specific domain."],"shared_structure":["Shift from individual intuition to procedural rigor","Trade-off between omission errors (expert) and commission errors (panel)"],"source_memory_refs":["SCR_002","SCR_004"],"transfer_claims":["Reliability is not just about the final answer but about the predictability and detectability of the failure mode."]},"claim":"A panel of trained non-experts following a checklist is more reliable than a single expert for tasks with verifiable outcomes because it replaces idiosyncratic cognitive failure (omission) with systemic, detectable failure (commission).","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task requires 'synthesis' rather than 'verification' (i.e., the checklist cannot capture the necessary emergent properties of the problem).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is so comprehensive that it induces 'compliance fatigue', leading the panel to check boxes without actual verification (The Checklist Paradox).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The checklist serves as an externalized memory and attention-steering mechanism that eliminates 'availability bias'\u2014where an expert overlooks a critical but non-salient factor\u2014while the panel structure provides a cross-verification layer that catches simple misinterpretations of checklist items.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
